evidence.snippet: Here, we report on 15 individuals from 14 families presenting with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, epilepsy, and structural brain anomalies, all of whom have extremely rare de novo mono-allelic or inherited bi-allelic variants in EIF4A2
evidence.explanation: Establishes EIF4A2 variants as the genetic lesion in the defining human cohort.

evidence.snippet: Molecular modeling predicts these variants would perturb structural interactions in key protein domains.
evidence.explanation: The predicted structural consequence of the variants is a computational (molecular-modelling) result, not a measurement.

evidence.snippet: DEAD-box proteins contain two conserved domains that both contribute to RNA and ATP binding.
evidence.explanation: Crystallographic work including the human eIF4A2 (DDX2B) DEAD domain establishes the two-domain architecture that the disease variants are predicted to perturb.

evidence.snippet: In more detail, missense and loss-of-function variants in EIF4A2 (DDX2B) are associated with the Neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and speech delay, with or without seizures (NEDHSS, #620455) (Paul et al., 2023).
evidence.explanation: An independent 2024 review states the variant classes (missense and loss of function) and confirms the gene-disease pairing; this is a review summary of other authors' work rather than primary data, hence OTHER.

steps/1.description: NEDHSS is caused by extremely rare de novo mono-allelic or inherited bi-allelic variants in EIF4A2, which encodes the DEAD-box ATP-dependent RNA helicase eIF4A2 (DDX2B). Molecular modelling of the reported variants predicts that they perturb structural interactions within key domains of the protein. DEAD-box helicases are built from two conserved RecA-like domains that jointly form the RNA- and ATP-binding surface, so substitutions within or between these domains are expected to alter RNA binding, ATP hydrolysis, or the coupling between them.

evidence.snippet: Overall, our findings reveal that EIF4A2 variants cause a genetic neurodevelopmental syndrome with both LOF and gain of function as underlying mechanisms.
evidence.explanation: The dual loss-of-function/gain-of-function conclusion is drawn from the Drosophila variant-rescue experiments, i.e. whole-organism model data.

evidence.snippet: In addition, only wild-type (WT), but not helicase activity dead mutants (DQAD and NEAD) of eIF4A2 (15), can rescue the eIF4A2 KD effects on ESC proliferation, morphology, and the expression of differentiation and 2C transcripts
evidence.explanation: Helicase-dead eIF4A2 fails to rescue eIF4A2 knockdown in cultured embryonic stem cells, establishing that the helicase activity - not merely the presence of the protein - is required.

steps/2.description: eIF4A2 uses ATP binding and hydrolysis to remodel RNA. The disease variants are predicted to perturb the interfaces that couple ATP hydrolysis to RNA duplex remodelling. Both loss and gain of function are proposed for different alleles: in the Drosophila rescue assay some variant cDNAs behaved as hypomorphs while others produced variant-specific defects not explained by simple loss of activity, and the discovery authors concluded that both mechanisms operate. The helicase activity itself is functionally required - helicase-dead eIF4A2 mutants fail to rescue eIF4A2 depletion in embryonic stem cells - so an activity lesion is mechanistically sufficient to matter.

evidence.snippet: In patient-derived fibroblasts, eIF4A2 production amounted to only 50% of the normal quantity.
evidence.explanation: Direct measurement of ~50% eIF4A2 protein in patient fibroblasts carrying a truncating EIF4A2 allele establishes haploinsufficiency.

evidence.snippet: By complementing the analyses with fibroblasts bearing EIF4A2 biallelic mutations, we established a correlation between IMP1 expression alterations and eIF4A2 functional dosage.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates that the downstream molecular readout scales with eIF4A2 dosage across heterozygous and bi-allelic patient cells.

evidence.snippet: In more detail, missense and loss-of-function variants in EIF4A2 (DDX2B) are associated with the Neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and speech delay, with or without seizures (NEDHSS, #620455) (Paul et al., 2023).
evidence.explanation: Justifies placing a protein-dosage node on the NEDHSS pathograph: the NEDHSS allelic spectrum explicitly includes loss-of-function variants, so the reduced-dosage state measured in EIF4A2-truncating patient cells is a mechanism that NEDHSS alleles can produce, even though the cells assayed came from the allelic dystonia families.

steps/3.description: Truncating EIF4A2 alleles reduce eIF4A2 protein abundance. In fibroblasts from carriers of the heterozygous frameshift deletion c.896_897del, eIF4A2 protein was reduced to approximately half of the normal level, establishing haploinsufficiency as a real, measurable consequence of truncating EIF4A2 alleles. The same study showed a dose-dependent relationship between eIF4A2 functional dosage and the downstream Ccr4-Not target IMP1 by comparing heterozygous and bi-allelic patient fibroblasts. These fibroblasts derive from the allelic dystonia-tremor syndrome rather than from NEDHSS probands, so this node states what reduced EIF4A2 dosage does to the translational machinery, not that dystonia is a NEDHSS feature.

evidence.snippet: Eukaryotic initiation factor-4A2 (EIF4A2) is an ATP-dependent RNA helicase and a member of the DEAD-box protein family that recognizes the 5' cap structure of mRNAs, allows mRNA to bind to the ribosome, and plays an important role in microRNA-regulated gene repression.
evidence.explanation: The discovery paper's statement of eIF4A2's normal role in cap-dependent initiation; this is a background summary of prior work, not a result of the study, hence OTHER.

evidence.snippet: Clamping of eIF4A to RNA causes steric blocks that interfere with ribosome binding and scanning, rationalizing the potency of these molecules since not all eIF4A molecules need to be engaged to elicit a biological effect.
evidence.explanation: Chemical-biology evidence that interfering with eIF4A function blocks ribosome recruitment and scanning, defining the step this node describes.

evidence.snippet: The binding peaks of eIF4A2 are enriched in mRNAs, particularly at 5′ untranslated region (5′UTR) and the immediate neighboring region of coding sequence (CDS), an mRNA translation initiation region (TIR) that is crucial for the regulation of translation initiation
evidence.explanation: eCLIP-seq localises eIF4A2 binding to the translation initiation region, the site at which this node acts.

evidence.snippet: eIF4A2 is a TIF, but its depletion did not alter global translation rates in ESCs
evidence.explanation: Constrains the claim: eIF4A2 loss changes which mRNAs are initiated rather than shutting down bulk translation, so the node is scoped to selective rather than global initiation failure.

steps/4.description: Within the eIF4F cap-binding complex, eIF4A resolves secondary structure in the 5' leader so that the 43S preinitiation complex can be loaded and can scan to the start codon; pharmacological clamping of eIF4A1/eIF4A2 onto RNA blocks exactly these steps. eIF4A2 recognises the 5' cap structure, permits mRNA loading onto the ribosome, and binds preferentially in the translation initiation region spanning the 5' UTR and the adjacent start of the coding sequence. Importantly, eIF4A2 loss does not collapse bulk protein synthesis - global translation rates are unchanged in eIF4A2-depleted cells - so the disease-relevant consequence is a shift in which mRNAs are efficiently initiated, not a general translational shutdown.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that eIF4A2 is a major effector of the repressive miRNA pathway functioning via the Ccr4-Not complex.
evidence.explanation: Establishes eIF4A2 as the principal Ccr4-Not-associated effector of miRNA-mediated repression.

evidence.snippet: eIF4A2 exerts its repressive effect by binding purine-rich motifs which are enriched in the 5'UTR of target mRNAs directly upstream of the AUG start codon.
evidence.explanation: Defines the cis-element through which eIF4A2 imposes repression at initiation.

evidence.snippet: We demonstrate that the DEAD-box helicases eIF4A2 and DDX6 interact directly with the MA3 and MIF domains of CNOT1 and compete for binding.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the physical interface between eIF4A2 and the Ccr4-Not scaffold CNOT1.

evidence.snippet: Together, these data show that the fate of an mRNA is dependent on the specific recruitment of either eIF4A2 or DDX6 to the CCR4-NOT complex which results in different pathways for translational repression and mRNA deadenylation.
evidence.explanation: Shows that eIF4A2 occupancy of Ccr4-Not determines whether a target mRNA is repressed or deadenylated, so losing eIF4A2 changes target mRNA fate.

evidence.snippet: Reduction of eIF4A2 was associated with abnormally increased levels of IMP1, a target of Ccr4-Not, the complex that interacts with eIF4A2 to mediate microRNA-dependent translational repression.
evidence.explanation: Patient-derived cells with an EIF4A2 variant show de-repression of a Ccr4-Not target, demonstrating that this arm is disrupted by human EIF4A2 lesions.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, eIF4A2 and Ccr4-Not displayed significantly diminished colocalization in dystonia patient cells.
evidence.explanation: Direct cellular evidence that the eIF4A2-Ccr4-Not assembly step itself is impaired when eIF4A2 is reduced.

steps/5.description: Separately from its activating role in eIF4F, eIF4A2 is a major effector of the repressive microRNA pathway. It binds the MA3 and MIF4G domains of CNOT1 - competing with DDX6 for the same site - and, once incorporated into Ccr4-Not, represses target mRNAs at the initiation step by binding purine-rich motifs in the 5' UTR immediately upstream of the AUG. Which helicase is recruited also determines the fate of the transcript: eIF4A2 inhibits CNOT7 deadenylase activity whereas DDX6 enhances it, so eIF4A2-bound mRNAs keep longer poly(A) tails. In EIF4A2-variant patient fibroblasts this arm is measurably broken: eIF4A2 and Ccr4-Not show significantly reduced colocalization and the Ccr4-Not target IMP1 is abnormally elevated.

evidence.snippet: We identified eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A2 (eIF4A2) and defined its mechanistic action through ribosomal protein S26-independent and -dependent ribosomes in translation initiation activation of messenger RNAs (mRNAs) encoding pluripotency factors and the histone variant H3.3 with demonstrated roles in maintaining stem cell pluripotency.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that eIF4A2 selectively activates translation of developmental-potency and chromatin transcripts.

evidence.snippet: Accordingly, knockdown of eIF4A2 disrupts ESC proteome, causing the loss of ESC identity.
evidence.explanation: Loss of eIF4A2 reshapes the proteome and changes cell identity, the cellular event this node describes.

evidence.snippet: The fruit fly homolog of EIF4A2 is eIF4A, a negative regulator of decapentaplegic (dpp) signaling that regulates embryo patterning, eye and wing morphogenesis, and stem cell identity determination.
evidence.explanation: Provides an independent developmental-program role for the eIF4A2 orthologue; support is partial because the pathway named (dpp) is an invertebrate developmental pathway and has not been shown to be the relevant output in human neurons.

steps/6.description: Because eIF4A2 both activates initiation on some transcripts and represses others via Ccr4-Not, its disruption reshapes a specific translational program rather than reducing protein output globally. In embryonic stem cells, eIF4A2 activates translation of pluripotency-factor and histone H3.3 mRNAs while restricting the totipotent two-cell program, and its knockdown disrupts the proteome and causes loss of cell identity - the clearest experimental demonstration that eIF4A2 dosage sets a developmental cell-fate program through translation. The disease-relevant claim, that the equivalent program in developing human neurons is what fails in NEDHSS, is an extension from stem-cell and invertebrate systems and is therefore provisional.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report on 15 individuals from 14 families presenting with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, epilepsy, and structural brain anomalies, all of whom have extremely rare de novo mono-allelic or inherited bi-allelic variants in EIF4A2
evidence.explanation: Structural brain anomalies are listed as a defining feature of the cohort.

evidence.snippet: One such disorder is EIF4A2-related neurodevelopmental disorder, a recently described disorder with various clinical associations, including developmental delay, epilepsy, and structural brain anomalies.
evidence.explanation: Independent confirmation that structural brain anomalies are part of the recognised clinical spectrum.

evidence.snippet: Out of the already established NDD-associated DExH/DEAD-box RNA helicase genes, EIF4A2 (DDX2B), DDX3X, DDX6 and DHX30, showed a strong expression during all developmental periods.
evidence.explanation: Human Brain Transcriptome database reanalysis shows EIF4A2 is strongly expressed in the developing human brain across embryonic, late fetal, neonatal and early childhood periods, which is the expression basis for a developmental brain phenotype. Tagged COMPUTATIONAL because it is a database reanalysis rather than a wet-lab measurement.

steps/7.description: Structural brain anomalies are one of the five defining features of the reported cohort and are documented on neuroimaging. A subsequent case series added absent cochlear nerve as a further structural finding, extending the malformation spectrum beyond the cerebrum to a cranial nerve.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report on 15 individuals from 14 families presenting with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, epilepsy, and structural brain anomalies, all of whom have extremely rare de novo mono-allelic or inherited bi-allelic variants in EIF4A2
evidence.explanation: Epilepsy is a defining feature of the cohort, establishing that an epileptogenic state arises in this disorder.

evidence.snippet: Both cases presented here involve patients who developed subtle, initially electrographically negative, epileptic spasms before going on to develop characteristic findings of infantile spasms requiring hormonal treatment.
evidence.explanation: Documents the specific epilepsy syndrome (evolution to infantile spasms) that this node produces.

steps/8.description: Epilepsy is one of the defining features of NEDHSS, and the reported seizure semiology includes epileptic spasms evolving into infantile spasms that required hormonal therapy. No EIF4A2-specific epileptogenic mechanism has been established: the node records that a hyperexcitable network state exists and produces the seizure phenotype, without asserting a validated molecular route from translational deregulation to hyperexcitability.

evidence.snippet: Neurodegeneration was predominantly reported in individuals with bi-allelic variants.
evidence.explanation: Direct statement that neurodegeneration segregates with the bi-allelic genotype group.

steps/9.description: Neurodegeneration was reported predominantly in the individuals carrying inherited bi-allelic EIF4A2 variants, distinguishing that arm from the largely static encephalopathy of the mono-allelic group. Because this is a clinical-radiological observation across a 15-person cohort rather than a neuropathological series, the node is provisional: no post-mortem or longitudinal imaging characterisation of the degenerative process exists.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report on 15 individuals from 14 families presenting with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, epilepsy, and structural brain anomalies, all of whom have extremely rare de novo mono-allelic or inherited bi-allelic variants in EIF4A2
evidence.explanation: Enumerates the organism-level clinical features that define the disorder.

steps/10.description: The organism-level convergence point of the disorder: global developmental delay, impaired intellectual development with poor or absent speech, gross and fine motor delay, and hypotonia, in most reported individuals at a severe level. This is the node from which the clinical phenotype layer of this entry is reached.

edges/3.description: Substitutions predicted to perturb the RNA- and ATP-binding domains directly compromise the helicase cycle of the protein.

edges/4.description: Frameshift and other truncating EIF4A2 alleles reduce the amount of eIF4A2 protein produced, a dosage rather than an activity lesion.

edges/5.description: Loss of the ATP-driven duplex-remodelling step directly impairs the preparation of structured 5' leaders for 43S preinitiation complex recruitment and scanning.

edges/6.description: The repressive arm of eIF4A2 also requires an intact protein able to engage RNA and CNOT1, so an activity lesion degrades repression as well as activation.

edges/7.description: Halving the eIF4A2 pool reduces the amount available to be incorporated into Ccr4-Not, and this was measured directly as reduced eIF4A2-Ccr4-Not colocalization with de-repression of the target IMP1.

edges/8.description: Altered initiation efficiency on eIF4A2-dependent transcripts changes the abundance of the proteins they encode.

edges/9.description: Failure to repress the correct set of transcripts changes the neuronal proteome in the opposite direction to the initiation defect, and the two arms together define the composite translational lesion.

edges/10.description: The specific translational targets that link the deregulated program to human cortical malformation have not been identified, so at least one required intermediate is unknown.

edges/11.description: Bi-allelic variants, which are expected to reduce eIF4A2 function most severely, are the group in which neurodegeneration is predominantly reported; the intervening cell-biological steps are unknown.

edges/12.description: Structural brain anomalies co-occur with epilepsy in this cohort and are a recognised generic substrate for seizures, but no EIF4A2-specific epileptogenic lesion has been characterised, so the intermediates are unknown.

edges/13.description: Abnormal brain structure is the tissue-level substrate of the global developmental delay, intellectual disability and motor impairment observed clinically.

edges/14.description: Refractory infantile spasms are themselves a developmental epileptic encephalopathy and compound the neurodevelopmental impairment.

edges/15.description: Superimposed neurodegeneration worsens the developmental phenotype and accounts for regression in the bi-allelic group.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report on 15 individuals from 14 families presenting with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, epilepsy, and structural brain anomalies, all of whom have extremely rare de novo mono-allelic or inherited bi-allelic variants in EIF4A2
evidence.explanation: The gene-disease association statement: 15 affected individuals from 14 unrelated families all carry ultra-rare EIF4A2 variants.

evidence.snippet: In comparison, the EIF4A2 variant cDNAs failed or incompletely rescued the lethality.
evidence.explanation: Functional in vivo evidence for variant pathogenicity from the Drosophila rescue assay.

evidence.snippet: Overall, our findings reveal that EIF4A2 variants cause a genetic neurodevelopmental syndrome with both LOF and gain of function as underlying mechanisms.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own summary of the mechanism class supported by their Drosophila data.

evidence.snippet: This search revealed nine RNA helicase genes, that can be regarded as definitely associated with a human disorders.
evidence.explanation: Independent 2024 expert review places EIF4A2 among the RNA helicase genes definitely associated with human disease, corroborating gene-disease validity beyond the single discovery cohort. Tagged OTHER because it is a review-level assessment, not primary patient data.

genes/0.notes: `variant_origin` is single-valued and is set to the predominant mode, DE_NOVO. It under-describes this gene: inherited bi-allelic variants and one mosaic proband are also reported. The full set of modes is curated in the three `inheritance` blocks (autosomal dominant de novo, autosomal recessive bi-allelic, somatic mosaicism), which is the authoritative statement for this entry.

evidence.snippet: Both cases presented here involve patients who developed subtle, initially electrographically negative, epileptic spasms before going on to develop characteristic findings of infantile spasms requiring hormonal treatment.
evidence.explanation: Documents that hormonal treatment for infantile spasms was required; support is PARTIAL because no response or outcome data are reported and the series describes the spasms as refractory.

treatments/0.description: Seizure management is empiric and syndrome-directed. Both patients in the 2026 pediatric series progressed to infantile spasms that required hormonal treatment (the standard first-line approach to infantile spasms), and the series title records the spasms as refractory. No EIF4A2-specific antiseizure strategy has been established and no efficacy data exist for this disorder. The practical implication of the reported course is that spasms should be looked for actively and treated promptly, not that any particular agent is preferred.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report on 15 individuals from 14 families presenting with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, epilepsy, and structural brain anomalies, all of whom have extremely rare de novo mono-allelic or inherited bi-allelic variants in EIF4A2
evidence.explanation: Establishes the developmental delay and hypotonia that motivate rehabilitation input; support is PARTIAL because the source reports no therapy or outcome data.

treatments/1.description: Because global developmental delay, hypotonia and poor or absent speech are the core disability, multidisciplinary developmental support - physical and occupational therapy for hypotonia and motor delay, and speech and alternative-communication support for the speech deficit - is the mainstay of care. No disorder-specific rehabilitation protocol has been published; this is standard practice for a severe global neurodevelopmental disorder and is curated here as supportive care rather than as an evidence-based disease-modifying intervention.

evidence.snippet: In this case series, we describe two patients with pathogenic EIF4A2 variants, including one of the first detailed reports of a patient with EIF4A2 mosaicism, to add to the growing catalog of genotypic variability in this disorder, as well as a novel phenotypic finding of absent cochlear nerve.
evidence.explanation: Documents the anatomical finding that makes audiological assessment necessary; support is PARTIAL because no audiological management is reported in the source.

treatments/2.description: Absent cochlear nerve has been reported in this disorder. Because a non-existent cochlear nerve is the one hearing-loss aetiology in which a cochlear implant cannot work, habilitation for an affected child may require an auditory brainstem implant or a visual/manual communication route rather than a cochlear implant. This is inference from the anatomical finding, not a reported intervention in an EIF4A2 patient. The diagnostic step that must precede any implantation decision - dedicated imaging of the internal auditory canal - is curated in `diagnosis` rather than here.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report on 15 individuals from 14 families presenting with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, epilepsy, and structural brain anomalies, all of whom have extremely rare de novo mono-allelic or inherited bi-allelic variants in EIF4A2
evidence.explanation: The coexistence of de novo mono-allelic and inherited bi-allelic inheritance in the same disorder is precisely what makes genotype-specific counselling necessary.

evidence.snippet: In this case series, we describe two patients with pathogenic EIF4A2 variants, including one of the first detailed reports of a patient with EIF4A2 mosaicism, to add to the growing catalog of genotypic variability in this disorder, as well as a novel phenotypic finding of absent cochlear nerve.
evidence.explanation: Reported mosaicism is the reason recurrence risk after an apparently de novo variant cannot be quoted as zero.

treatments/3.description: Counselling must be genotype-specific in this disorder because the two modes of inheritance carry very different recurrence risks: a de novo mono-allelic variant implies a low (but non-zero, given reported mosaicism) recurrence risk, whereas inherited bi-allelic variants imply a 25% recurrence risk for future pregnancies. The reported mosaic proband is the reason parental mosaicism cannot be assumed absent.

evidence.snippet: Overall, our findings reveal that EIF4A2 variants cause a genetic neurodevelopmental syndrome with both LOF and gain of function as underlying mechanisms.
evidence.explanation: The dual-mechanism conclusion that the gap asks to resolve at allele resolution.

open_questions/0.rationale: The discovery paper concludes that both loss and gain of function operate, but the assignment rests on a Drosophila rescue assay scoring pupal lethality and variant-specific behavioural and developmental defects. No biochemical measurement of ATPase or helicase activity, RNA binding, or eIF4F/Ccr4-Not incorporation has been reported for any patient allele. Until that is done the direction of effect for a newly identified variant cannot be predicted, which blocks both variant interpretation and any dosage-based therapeutic reasoning. This is the load-bearing mechanistic uncertainty in the entry.

evidence.snippet: Accordingly, knockdown of eIF4A2 disrupts ESC proteome, causing the loss of ESC identity.
evidence.explanation: The model result whose transfer to human neurons is unvalidated: the identity program measured is pluripotency, not neurodevelopment.

evidence.snippet: mice lacking eIF4A2 are viable, whereas those lacking eIF4A1 are not, indicating the latter to be essential
evidence.explanation: Sharpens the mismatch: the constitutive mouse Eif4a2 knockout is viable and has not been reported to model the human neurodevelopmental phenotype, so the obvious rodent model does not obviously fit.

open_questions/1.rationale: Every functional characterisation of what eIF4A2 does to a developmental program comes from a non-human, non-neuronal system: mouse embryonic stem cells (pluripotency factors, histone H3.3, Zscan4) and Drosophila (dpp signalling, wing and eye morphogenesis). The one human-cell dataset is fibroblasts from the allelic dystonia families, assaying a single Ccr4-Not target. No human neuron, cortical organoid, or patient iPSC-derived neural model of EIF4A2 has been reported, and no neuronal translatome has been measured. This is a translational-validity question rather than a simple absence of evidence: the model data exist and are strong, but the mRNA targets that matter are cell-type-specific by the models' own logic, so their transfer to human neurons is the open question. It matters because the identity of the mis-translated neuronal transcripts is what any mechanism-directed therapy would have to act on.

evidence.snippet: Both cases presented here involve patients who developed subtle, initially electrographically negative, epileptic spasms before going on to develop characteristic findings of infantile spasms requiring hormonal treatment.
evidence.explanation: The specific, unexplained epilepsy phenotype the gap is about.

open_questions/2.rationale: Epilepsy is a defining feature and the reported semiology (electrographically negative spasms evolving to refractory infantile spasms) is specific enough to be mechanistically informative, yet nothing is known about how EIF4A2 dysfunction produces it. Neither the structural-lesion hypothesis nor an independent excitability hypothesis has been tested, and no electrophysiology in any EIF4A2 model has been reported. Resolving this would determine whether antiseizure choice should follow the structural-epilepsy playbook or something disorder-specific.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, we demonstrate that the inability to sumoylate eIF4A2 results in impaired stress granule formation, indicating a new role for sumoylation in the stress response.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that eIF4A2 is required for normal stress granule formation; support is PARTIAL because the link to NEDHSS neurodegeneration is hypothetical and the experiments used a sumoylation-site mutant, not a patient allele.

evidence.snippet: Neurodegeneration was predominantly reported in individuals with bi-allelic variants.
evidence.explanation: The clinical observation the hypothesis is trying to explain.

evidence.snippet: Aberrant formation of stress granules is an important feature of NDD associated pathogenic variants in DHX30 and DDX3x (Lessel et al., 2017; Lennox et al., 2020; Mannucci et al., 2021).
evidence.explanation: Establishes that aberrant stress granule formation is an established disease mechanism for two other neurodevelopmental RNA-helicase genes, which is the precedent that makes the hypothesis worth testing for EIF4A2. Tagged OTHER because it is a review statement about other authors' findings.

open_questions/3.rationale: eIF4A2 is sumoylated at K226 and is recruited to stress granules, and cells unable to sumoylate eIF4A2 form stress granules poorly. Defective stress granule dynamics is a recurring theme in neurodegeneration, which makes this an attractive candidate route to the degenerative arm of NEDHSS that is absent from the mono-allelic group. The hypothesis is explicitly untested in this disease: no patient allele has been assayed for stress granule behaviour, no reported variant affects K226, and the stress granule work was done in unrelated cell lines. It is recorded as an emerging hypothesis, not curated as a pathophysiology node.

evidence.snippet: Here, we report on 15 individuals from 14 families presenting with global developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, epilepsy, and structural brain anomalies, all of whom have extremely rare de novo mono-allelic or inherited bi-allelic variants in EIF4A2
evidence.explanation: Defines the cohort size that limits every frequency and natural-history statement in this entry.

open_questions/4.rationale: The entity rests on a single 15-person cohort plus a two-patient series. Frequencies in this entry are therefore small-denominator estimates derived from a group-level presenting-features sentence; several features named in OMIM and MedGen (poor or absent speech, inability to walk, tube feeding) could not be given an independent numerator from any abstract-level source and are curated here without frequency bands. Adult outcomes are unknown, and whether the mono-allelic and bi-allelic arms differ in anything beyond neurodegeneration cannot be assessed.

evidence.snippet: Human ornithine aminotransferase (hOAT) is a mitochondrial matrix pyridoxal‐5′‐phosphate enzyme (PLP) that catalyzes the reversible transfer of the δ‐amino group of L‐ornithine (L‐Orn) to α‐ketoglutarate (α‐KG) yielding glutamate‐5‐semialdehyde (GSA) and glutamate.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports the primary enzymatic function disrupted in OAT deficiency.

evidence.snippet: OAT is mainly involved in ornithine catabolism in adults, thus explaining the hyperornithinemia as hallmark of the disease.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the role of OAT in ornithine catabolism and its link to the disease hallmark of hyperornithinemia.

evidence.snippet: The deficit of hOAT leads to a 10-to-15 fold increase in the plasmatic L-Orn concentration, along with a small reduction in the levels of glutamate, glutamine, lysine and creatine
evidence.explanation: Review text supports elevated L-ornithine and secondary reductions in glutamate, lysine, and creatine downstream of hOAT deficiency.

steps/1.description: OAT deficiency disrupts mitochondrial matrix, PLP-dependent ornithine transamination, blocking L-ornithine catabolism to glutamate semialdehyde/P5C and glutamate and causing the metabolic defect underlying gyrate atrophy.

evidence.snippet: All patients had high plasma ornithine levels at the time of diagnosis, and they were all started on an arginine-restricted diet.
evidence.explanation: This directly supports hyperornithinemia as the key metabolic intermediate between OAT deficiency and retinal degeneration.

evidence.snippet: Deficiency of ornithine-delta-aminotransferase (OAT) in humans results in gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina (GA), an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by ornithine accumulation and a progressive chorioretinal degeneration of unknown pathogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Mouse model study confirms ornithine accumulation as the characteristic biochemical feature of OAT deficiency.

steps/2.description: Loss of ornithine aminotransferase activity causes marked plasma ornithine accumulation, the central biochemical lesion in the disease.

evidence.snippet: The deficit of hOAT leads to a 10-to-15 fold increase in the plasmatic L-Orn concentration, along with a small reduction in the levels of glutamate, glutamine, lysine and creatine
evidence.explanation: Review text supports secondary reductions in amino-acid and creatine pools downstream of hOAT deficiency.

evidence.snippet: the increased ornithine level is the clinical manifestation of gyrate atrophy of choroid and retina, muscle weakness, moderate mental retardation, and low cerebral creatine.
evidence.explanation: Case-report abstract supports low cerebral creatine alongside extraocular neurologic and neuromuscular manifestations.

steps/3.description: The OAT metabolic lesion is accompanied by reduced glutamate, lysine, and creatine pools; low cerebral creatine provides a plausible biochemical link to extraocular neurologic and neuromuscular manifestations in a subset of patients.

evidence.snippet: At 2 mo, the retinal pigment epithelium is histologically normal, but electron microscopy reveals sporadic degeneration of scattered pigment epithelial cells.

evidence.snippet: Our results indicate that retinal pigment epithelial cells are the initial site of insult in GA and that the OAT-deficient mouse is an excellent animal model of GA in human patients.
evidence.explanation: The study identifies RPE cells as the initial injury site in the disease model.

steps/4.description: Retinal pigment epithelial cells are an early site of insult in the hyperornithinemic OAT-deficient retina, preceding progressive photoreceptor disorganization and cell loss.

evidence.snippet: The patients primarily present with progressive ophthalmological findings.
evidence.explanation: This cohort study directly supports progressive ophthalmologic degeneration as the key downstream disease process.

evidence.snippet: an arginine-restricted diet substantially reduces plasma ornithine levels and completely prevents retinal degeneration in Oat(-/-)
evidence.explanation: Mouse model demonstrates that reducing ornithine accumulation prevents retinal degeneration, confirming that hyperornithinemia drives chorioretinal damage.

evidence.snippet: Our results indicate that retinal pigment epithelial cells are the initial site of insult in GA and that the OAT-deficient mouse is an excellent animal model of GA in human patients.
evidence.explanation: Mouse-model evidence identifies RPE cells as the initial cellular site of injury in gyrate atrophy.

evidence.snippet: Like human GA patients, adult OAT-deficient mice exhibit chronic hyperornithinemia to levels 10-15-fold above normal and massive ornithinuria. open_questions/0.rationale: Ornithine accumulates in every tissue, yet the ophthalmic phenotype dominates the clinical picture. Candidate explanations have included ornithine-driven inhibition of creatine synthesis with consequent phosphocreatine depletion in a highly energy-demanding tissue, and proline deficiency in the retinal pigment epithelium, but neither is established. This is not merely descriptive: an ornithine threshold below which the retina is safe would let treatment be titrated to a target, and the observation that field decline stabilized below 500 micromolar in one advanced case hints at such a threshold without establishing one.
